Why move to header file ?

.c file is > 650LOC and my preference is for smaller files.  I realize breaking that up further wasn't really the pattern here with wireshark, but I saw other dissectors doing this (packet-icmp.h for example), so I went as far as I felt followed the existing pattern.

Not a hill I want to die on or anything, can merge if that is asked.

I am all for breaking up some of the larger files (e.g., moving PFCP vendor IEs that register to a table to a separate file), but it seems a bit premature if it's not being used by another source file yet, and in any case should probably be a separate MR.
The time for code review of a MR generally scales worse than O(N) where N is SLOC.

Okay, I don't have any intentions to make any further modifications at this time- other than to address any new feedback items.

You cannot use `col_set_str` here. `col_set_str` does a shallow copy of the `char *` pointer and cannot be used with a char array declared on the stack. You could get `col_add_str` (which copies it), but it would be better to use `col_add_fstr(pinfo->cinfo, COL_INFO, "%s Reply", roon_service_name)` instead of using snprintf.
(You also can't use `col_set_str` with `wmem_packet_scope()` declared strings, but `pinfo->pool` has exactly the correct, slightly longer, lifetime.)

changed this line in [version 12 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/20575/diffs?diff_id=1429783523&start_sha=837c9317450db8fe06810e6dbcc8066a6b2578ba#512d386e10e9a98c0a628bc089663ec6813bbe55_321_323)
This is, incidentally, the same as `ascii_strdown_inplace` from `wsutil/str_util.h`.

changed this line in [version 12 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/20575/diffs?diff_id=1429783523&start_sha=837c9317450db8fe06810e6dbcc8066a6b2578ba#512d386e10e9a98c0a628bc089663ec6813bbe55_333_330)

On average it might make sense to lowercase value once (perhaps with `wmem_ascii_strdown(pinfo->pool, value, -1)`) once and then have the comparisons be case-sensitive, at least if the entries in the const array are guaranteed to be lowercase. The lowercased version could be saved for the tid, if appropriate.

With the caveat that I am reverse engineering this protocol so I don't have 100% understanding...

Basically, these service_id UUID values are usually lowercase, but occasionally seeing them uppercase.  So far it sees to be consistent for a given UUID, but not sure if that is version/platform specific or something like that.  They also have multiple SDK's (C, Javascript, not sure about others?) so might be related to that.

Anyways, right now I've decided to normalize the service_id's for processing, but display the original raw value.  If I understand your comment correctly, your proposed optimization would lower case the `value` in the protocol tree which I do not want to happen due to the ambiguity described above.
Fair enough.
